newsitem.title: UK: Dollar steady in late Europe but drifts off highs.
newsitem.headline: Dollar steady in late Europe but drifts off highs.

text.p: The dollar was steady against the mark and yen in late European trade, but off earlier highs and largely unshaken by a larger than expected rise in U.S. producer price data for October.
"Dollar/mark is established above the 1.50 mark level. The PPI figures don't seem to have had any dramatic effect," said Gwyn Hacche, senior economist at HSBC James Capel.

The producer price index rose 0.4 percent, exceeding forecasts of a 0.2 percent increase. The core PPI, which excludes higher energy prices and food, fell by 0.3 percent against expectations of a 0.1 percent increase.

The data were released as markets awaited the outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting, which began at 1400 GMT. Few expect action by the Federal Reserve on interest rates after this meeting.
At 1633 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.5040/45 marks after an afternoon high around 1.5080 marks. It stood at 1.5071/76 late Tuesday in Europe.

After hitting a two-month low of just below 1.49 marks on Tuesday, the dollar crossed the 1.50 psychological barrier on the same day after a round of pro-dollar remarks by a series of Bundesbank officials.

"The dollar's come off the ropes in the past couple of days. I think we're seeing tentative signs of a recovery, but it's not through the worst of its troubles in the short term," said Bear Stearns' chief economist David Brown.
"Obviously it's been given a bit of a leg up by the Bundesbank. The Bundesbank cannot really afford to have a radically stronger mark," said Brown.

Bundesbank council members Olaf Sievert and Franz-Christoph Zeitler said on Wednesday current German interest rates were appropriate but that it was not necessarily the end of a cycle of interest rate cuts.
Five other senior bank officials, including president Hans Tietmeyer, are scheduled to speak later this week which analysts expect will see more Bundesbank verbal support for the dollar.

"Everyone is expecting the same comments from the rest (of the Buba members), so it's hard to see them having more impact," a Japanese bank trader said. "What people are looking for now is for one of them to say something different."
Against the yen, the dollar was trading at 111.32/42 compared with 111.68/73 late Tuesday.
Eisuke Sakakibara, director general of the Ministry of Finance's international finance bureau, is scheduled to speak at 0830 GMT on Thursday.
"The key is to see if we can get any statements out of the Ministry of Finance, over whether Japanese foreign policy has really changed," said Bear Stearns' Brown.
Markets were still wary about a strengthening yen after Sakakibara's comments last week that the dollar's correction from its 1995 lows against the yen was about to end.
